Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the VitalMed Devices, Inc. Third Quarter 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Alex Rivera, CEO; Mike Patel, CFO; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; and Jennifer Brooks, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. VitalMed Devices delivered outstanding results this quarter, powered by accelerating adoption of our cutting-edge medical devices and key strategic collaborations.

Today, I will cover five key aspects of our performance:
1. SG&A expense management and efficiency gains
2. Impact of pricing and cost management initiatives
3. Overall performance highlights and key achievements
4. R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress
5. Procedure volume trends and market recovery commentary

Mike will then provide a deeper dive into our financials. After that, we'll open the call for your questions.

Let's begin with our overall performance highlights and key achievements, which really set the stage for everything else.

I'm thrilled to start with these highlights, which highlight another quarter of outstanding execution in a fast-evolving medical devices arena. Headline figures first: we posted record quarterly revenue of $2.85 billion, up 14% year-over-year and 12% organically, surpassing our guidance midpoint of $2.75 billion. This is our 11th straight quarter of double-digit organic growth, fueled by solid demand in our main areas—cardiovascular, orthopedics, and neuromodulation—despite challenges like ongoing raw material inflation and some regional dips in elective procedures.

Adjusted EPS reached $1.62, up 22% from last year, thanks to our focused margin expansion efforts. Gross margins climbed 210 basis points to 68.5%, thanks to a positive shift toward high-margin consumables and productivity from rolling out SmartFactory 2.0 automation at our sites in Galway, Ireland, and Plymouth, Minnesota. Operating margins rose to 28.2%, gaining 150 basis points, as we captured $85 million in cost synergies from the NeuroPulse Therapeutics acquisition last year, beating our $300 million full-year goal.

Diving deeper into top-line drivers, cardiovascular—42% of revenue—jumped 18% organically to $1.21 billion. Our VitalFlow Ultra next-gen TAVR platform grabbed 22% U.S. market share in structural heart, adding 400 basis points on rivals like Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien and Medtronic's Evolut, backed by 95% one-year durability from the VitalFlow IDE trial presented at TCT 2023. Overseas, CE Mark expansions for peripheral interventions fueled 25% growth in EMEA, making us the number-two in drug-eluting stents behind Boston Scientific.

Orthopedics grew 11% to $785 million, hitting a milestone with FDA clearance for the Trinity Robotics System, our AI-driven navigation that pairs with robotic arm technology like Mako. Initial sites saw 30% shorter surgeries and 15% better implant precision in knee replacements, helping us gain 2 points of share in U.S. hips and knees to 18%, with procedures rebounding from COVID backlogs.

Neuromodulation advanced 16% to $485 million, driven by the U.S. launch of Rejuva DBS for Parkinson's, with adaptive algorithms via our ML-based VitalSense platform cutting battery use by 40% versus Abbott's Infinity. Remote monitoring attach rates hit 28%, lifting recurring revenue to 35% of the segment.

By region, U.S. led with 16% organic growth, aided by CMS 2024 IPPS preserving pass-through for premium EP catheters. EMEA grew 13% despite EU MDR hurdles, with 85% of our portfolio certified ahead of competitors. APAC surged 20%, fastest region, with China up 35% post-NMPA nod for VitalFlow Ultra and distributor partnerships like Intuitive Surgical's. Emerging markets added 8%, with low-cost ortho implants winning in high-volume cases.

Strategically, our VitalEdge program—$500 million over multiple years for digital therapeutics and supply chain strength—is ahead of plan. Edge AI covers 60% of U.S. cath labs, boosting AFib ablation outcomes 12% and targeting 25% CAGR for connected devices. R&D up 18% to $420 million, or 14.8% of revenue, backs 12 Phase III/IDE programs, like our bioresorbable coronary stent disrupting permanent implants akin to Abbott's old BVS.

Balance sheet strong: $650 million operating cash flow, up 25%, funding $400 million buybacks and 10% dividend increase to $0.65/share. Debt-to-EBITDA at 1.8x leaves room for M&A in structural heart wearables.

These outcomes confirm our edge in a 5-7% CAGR industry through 2028 per Evaluate MedTech, driven by demographics, value-based care, robotics, and neuromod. We're lifting full-year organic growth guide to 13-15% and adjusted EPS to $6.45-$6.55, confident in 10%+ long-term compounding.

Next, procedure volume trends and market recovery.

These trends are central to our top-line momentum. Global volumes across our portfolio rose 14% year-over-year in Q3, our sixth straight double-digit quarter, with year-to-date now 13% above 2019 pre-pandemic baselines. This captures strong elective recovery in structural heart, rhythm management, orthopedics, and endoscopy, from pent-up demand, better staffing, and gains in transcatheter and robotic procedures.

By franchise: Structural heart volumes soared 28% YoY, beating the market, via Evolut PRO+ TAVR grabbing 22% U.S. share in intermediate/high-risk cases. Low-risk expansions push U.S. to 105% of 2019. Europe grew 19% with Sapien Ultra CE Marks, though bovine pericardium supply nipped upside.

Rhythm management: Pacemaker/ICD implants up 11%, Micra leadless up 35% post-pediatric/MRI labels. AFib ablations +16% with pulsed-field catheter ramping in early markets.

Orthopedics: Hip/knee replacements +12%, Triathlon knee +15% in outpatient shift. Cementless now 45% mix from 32%, aiding recovery amid labor issues.

Endoscopy: +9%, GI at 98% pre-COVID, led by single-use duodenoscopes post-scandals.

Regions: U.S. (62% revenue) +18%, electives at 102% of 2019 per our Vizient/Premier data. ASCs now 28% of ortho/endoscopy volumes from 20%, via CMS MS-DRG boosts.

Europe (22%) +10%, NHS/DRG drags but Italy/France TAVR +25%, at 95% 2019 levels, MDR favoring us.

China/APAC (10%) +8%, China structural heart doubled post-NMPA, lockdowns easing.

Emerging (6%) +22%, LATAM ortho, India endoscopy for TB.

Recovery now pegged at 107% of 2019 by year-end from 104%. OR utilization 85% vs. 65% in 2022, CMS IPPS +3.2% TAVR pay. Headwinds: burnout, nitinol/PEEK inflation, offset by vertical laser-cutting.

We're pushing innovations: $250 million R&D for AI procedure planning with Hugo RAS, pilots showing 15% faster times, 12% volume boost. NeuroPace buy positions in $5B epilepsy (20% growth). da Vinci partnerships add $2B TAM.

This signals lasting recovery, raising full-year volumes to 12-14%, revenue $28.5-29.0 billion.

I'll now turn the call over to Mike Patel for insights on SG&A expense management, pricing and cost initiatives, and our broader financial review.

Mike Patel:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex outlined, we achieved robust financials this quarter.

Let me first address SG&A expense management and efficiency gains, where we've sustained strong progress despite macro pressures like inflation in professional services and logistics. In med devices, SG&A peers at 25-35% of revenue—Medtronic, Stryker, Boston Scientific—strained by sales forces, compliance, marketing for neurovascular stents, TAVR valves, robotic systems like da Vinci.

Q3 SG&A was $465 million, up 2% YoY reported, flat sequentially, under midpoint guide of $475 million. At 27.5% of revenue, that's 425 bps better than 31.8% last year, our best leverage in five years. Fifth straight quarter contracting from 35.2% pandemic peak, over $190 million cumulative run-rate savings from LeanOps 2025 launched early 2023.

Key drivers: Sales force optimization/digital (45% savings)—our 4,200 reps critical for IDNs/ASCs in value-based shifts. Salesforce Einstein AI for territory planning, propensity scoring lifted productivity 14% YoY (revenue/rep), topping Abbott's 8-10%. VR demos for EmbolicFlow coils cut travel 22%, $29 million Q3 save, close rates 68%.

U.S. (52% revenue) offset GPO pricing via Vizient/Premier, CMS IPPS. EMEA CRM harmonized 15 countries cut admin 18%, vs. BD MDR costs. APAC AI localized for China/India +25% efficiency amid yuan/tenders.

Procurement/indirect (30%)—SAP Ariba centralized $330 million spend, 16% save on labor, agencies, freight (7-10% inflation). Renegotiated packaging/labeling like Stryker, 15% back-office to Mexico/Poland: $23 million Q3, $95 million annual run-rate.

G&A/overhead (25%)—AWS cloud/RPA cut 11% YoY to $115 million. Litigation fees -30%, cyber for PercuNav IP. Headcount steady 12,500, attrition trims non-core, hires in digital analytics.

These are structural, targeting mid-teens op margins to 2025 despite U.S. elective softness, BWHC shortages, IRA taxes. 20% savings ($37 million) reinvested: AI marketing for neuromod, Epic data lakes like Intuitive's MyIntuitive.

U.S. leverage from reps, EMEA post-MDR (2% SG&A capex peak), APAC e-com for SE Asia consumables (9% CAGR Evaluate). Q4 SG&A $470-480 million, 27-28% revenue, 100-200 bps leverage.

This discipline boosts FCF to 110% net income, funding innovation in $550B market.

Shifting to impact of pricing and cost management, core to our 8% organic growth, 220 bps gross margin expansion to 67.8%, EBITDA margins 28.5%. Amid titanium/polymer inflation (12% ISM), CMS site-neutral, we protected profits for mid-teens FY24 EPS.

Pricing first: 4.2% ASP rise constant currency, above Leerink 2-3%. Multi-prong for CV (45% rev, TAVR like Edwards Sapien), Ortho (30%, OrthoBot vs. Stryker Mako), Neuro (15%, like Medtronic InterStim).

AI pricing analytics on U.S. GPO real-time, 5.8% CV uplift passing 70% list inflation, 95% RFP wins vs. Abbott stent erosion.

Mix shift +300 bps: TAVR +15% to 25% CV, OrthoBot +22% ASCs at 20% premium post-No Surprises.

Regions: U.S. (65%) +5.1% offset 3% Medicare ortho cuts, value contracts 2x volume. Europe (20%) +2.9% vs. NICE/IQWiG, dossiers show 15% patency vs. Boston Eluvia, premium France/Benelux. EM (15%) +3.5% tiered, China neuro +18% NMPA.

Pricing added ~$185 million, 55% organic.

Costs: $220 million annual savings, COGS -180 bps amid resin +15%, titanium +10%, labor 6%.

Supply chain: 40% vertical (catheter polymers), 8% supplier cut, diversify Asia, 3-year deals 5% below, turns 5.2x from 4.1x, $120M WC.

Manufacturing: Six Sigma 12% yields, $150M FY23 cobots +18% throughput, -10% labor. Galway neuromod 99% OEE like da Vinci.

Indirect: R&D productivity +15% AI design (stent geo), 11% rev. ZBB SG&A -7% headcount offshore India $45M.

Regions: U.S./PR 60% FDA/site shifts. Europe 20% energy solar Dutch vs. CBAM. APAC Thailand local -25% forex.

Margins to 67.8%, +100-150 bps FY24.

Ahead: Value-based bundles TAVR/rehab 10-15% premium, 20% readmits cut (50K procedures). Japan PMDA pilots.

4:1 pricing-cost leverage vs. Zimmer ortho wars. 3-5% ASP, $250M+ savings FY24 fund 10% R&D AI robotics/bioresorbables.

Now, broader financials: Revenue $2.85B as Alex said. Expenses controlled, net income strong. Guidance: FY23 revenue $28.5-29.0B, EPS $6.45-6.55. Q4 SG&A as above, margins hold.

I'll hand to Dr. Vasquez for R&D and pipeline.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Mike. Excited to update on our innovation pipeline. We recently received FDA clearance for the Aria Surgical System, a groundbreaking single-port robotic platform for gynecology and general surgery that promises to revolutionize ambulatory procedures with superior usability and AI-driven precision.

As we close a solid quarter at $2.8 billion revenue—up 11% reported, 14% organic—our R&D investments and pipeline advances stand out. In a $600 billion market at 5-6% CAGR to 2028 per Grand View, R&D is key to beating Medtronic/Boston Scientific amid inflation, FDA PMA rigor.

Q3 R&D $485 million, 17.3% revenue, from 16.1% YoY, +13% or $55M seq. FY23 track $1.95B +15%, 42% new products, 28% sustaining, 20% clinical/reg, rest digital/M&A. Fits value-based/outpatient shift, AI/remote devices at 20-30% premiums like Abbott Libre/Medtronic Guardian.

Pipeline: 14 programs, five late-stage vs. three last year.

Structural heart: EvoFlow 3.0 TAVR (22% U.S. share Millennium) finished 800-patient IDE early, Q1 2024 IDE, 2025 PMA. 15% less leak, 20% faster vs. Sapien 3 Ultra. CE Mark MDR mid-market launches Germany/Nordics +25% EU rev seq.

Robotics/endoluminal: Aria hit 95% usability first-human, partnerships three U.S. ASCs beta. $120M YTD AI haptics/tissue predict, 2026 launch $25B market IDG.

Neuromod: ReNeuve SCS chronic pain—directional burst/closed-loop—FDA Breakthrough, cuts 12 months. NANS data 68% 12-month responders +10pts Nevro HF10. China NMPA bridge H2 2025 $2B APAC 12% CAGR.

Digital/wearables: CardioLink CGM-IPG hybrid Phase II, 250 patients 25 sites, 92% adherence, Apple/myMedTech subs like Dexcom G7.

Leveraging 65+ demo +20% U.S. 2030, CMS readmits. Bioresorb Absorbix 95% resorption 24 months no thrombosis vs. Abbott Absorb. $150M AI JDA imaging, EP bolt-ons.

Regions: U.S. 60% MDUFA V, Europe 25% MDR Class III compliant, APAC 15% Shanghai hub NMPA.

Forward: 17% intensity 2024, three approvals, four readouts, two rev starts. De-risks 8-10% growth, 25%+ EPS CAGR.

Now, back to Alex for Q&A.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Elena. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: press star one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Thanks, good morning. Alex, congrats on the quarter. Can you expand on the key drivers behind the 14% organic growth, especially how overall performance ties into market share gains across franchises?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, John. Absolutely, as I highlighted, it's broad-based. Cardiovascular led with 18% growth from VitalFlow Ultra's share grabs—400 bps in structural heart on superior durability data. Orthopedics and neuromod followed with robotics clearance and DBS launch momentum. Regionally, APAC's 20% acceleration via China approvals was huge. Mix toward premiums and procedure rebound added tailwinds. We're executing on VitalEdge digital push, confident in sustained momentum.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
Hi, thanks. Mike, on SG&A and pricing/cost—impressive leverage there. How sustainable are these gains with inflation and potential reimbursement changes? Any color on Q4 trajectory?

Mike Patel:
Great question, Emily. Sustainability is baked in via LeanOps structural changes. Rep productivity +14% from AI tools, procurement 16% savings on indirects—these aren't temporary. Pricing 4.2% ASP outpace with dynamic models, mix shifts, even in Europe HTA. Costs via vertical integration, automation hold GM upside. Q4 SG&A 27-28%, continued leverage despite comps. Inflation offset, positioning for mid-teens margins.

Alex Rivera:
Thanks for that insight, Mike.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Morning, team. Jennifer, on procedure volumes—strong recovery, but uneven regions. What's your commercial view on U.S. ASC shift and APAC potential, any pricing pushback?

Jennifer Brooks:
Hi, David. Volumes at 102% U.S. 2019, ASCs to 28% ortho/endoscopy on CMS boosts—surgeons love our OrthoBot premiums for outpatient. Commercial teams targeting high-volume IDNs with outcomes data, value contracts doubling uptake. APAC, China doubling structural heart post-lockdowns, tiered pricing scales volumes without erosion. Minimal pushback as evidence supports 15-20% better outcomes. Expect acceleration.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for that insight, Jennifer.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong:
Thanks. Elena, pipeline looks deep—EvoFlow 3.0, Aria milestones. Any updates on timelines or regulatory risks, especially MDR/NMPA?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, Lisa. Timelines on track: EvoFlow IDE Q1 2024, superior leak/deployment data de-risks PMA. Aria beta strong, 2026 launch. Breakthrough on ReNeuve accelerates. MDR fully compliant Class III, ahead peers; NMPA bridge studies progressing Shanghai hub. Risks managed via partnerships, real-world data. This fuels 8-10% growth.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. Before we conclude, I want to thank our employees, customers, and partners for their continued support. We are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
